items.title: Blocking Gut Cannabinoid Receptors Restores Memory in Fragile X
items.snippet: Can treating the gut restore memory in fragile X syndrome? Researchers discovered blocking peripheral cannabinoid (CB1) receptors outside the brain repairs the intestinal barrier, restores beneficial gut microbes, and improves hippocampal memory.

items.title: Brain’s Insula Shapes Pain, Emotion, and the Placebo Effect
items.snippet: How do emotions and expectations change the way you feel physical pain? Drawing on 15 years of intracranial brain recordings across 87 patients, neuroscientists mapped four distinct regions of the human insula, uncovering a top-down circuit behind the placebo effect.

items.title: Screen Time and Fitness Reshape Grey Matter in Teen Brains
items.snippet: How do smartphones and exercise shape the developing teenage brain? MRI scans show that heavy leisure screen time is linked to smaller grey matter volume in memory hubs—and may delay normal synaptic pruning in frontal decision-making regions.

items.title: Is free will an illusion? New brain research reveals a surprising twist
items.snippet: New research reveals that the brain makes free choices and forced decisions using surprisingly similar neural processes, with activity building toward a decision before we act. The discovery challenges assumptions about free will while suggesting that our personal preferences and experiences still shape what we choose.

items.title: Too much exercise could leave your brain stuck in overdrive
items.snippet: Exercising too much without adequate recovery may disrupt brain chemistry in surprising ways. Scientists found that mice subjected to prolonged, intense training had elevated dopamine levels in a brain region linked to memory and emotions, even 48 hours after exercising.
